separate liability, management, formality, and tax questions

claims.claim: The SBA says business structure can affect operations, personal-asset exposure, taxes, fundraising capacity, and paperwork, while state rules can vary.
A sole proprietorship does not create a separate business entity, according to the SBA.
The IRS describes a partnership as two or more people conducting business and sharing profits and losses.
An LLC is allowed by state statute, and IRS federal tax classification can vary with member count and elections.
The SBA describes a corporation as a legal entity separate from its owners and notes relatively extensive recordkeeping, operational processes, and reporting.
Actual entity, liability, governance, and tax conclusions require jurisdiction- and fact-specific review rather than a universal rule.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Business-structure labels and consequences vary by jurisdiction and may use different rules outside the United States.
positions: SBA offers a U.S. high-level comparison and warns state rules vary.
IRS explains U.S. federal tax treatment of LLCs.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson names the U.S. context of the sources, uses only high-level distinctions, and directs real decisions to relevant local authorities and qualified professionals.
